findings.evidence: The purpose list is a good procedure, but the thinking prompt is only the reader test: 'what will the reader do in their first 10 seconds'.

findings.evidence: Gotchas give reasons for vague subjects, unconfirmed dates, unasked CCs and hedged facts, but 'bullets only for 3-5 parallel points (never more)' and 'keep paragraphs to 2-3 sentences' state the limit without a why.
findings.fix: Add the reason already used for walls of text: more than five bullets or a paragraph past three sentences hides the ask, so the reader replies with a question instead of a decision.

findings.evidence: description: 'Draft or rewrite a professional email ... even without the word email. Produces a subject and body to paste; never sends. Not for casual chat replies'.
findings.fix: Draft or rewrite a professional email to a peer, stakeholder, manager or leadership using What-Why-How: subject line, ask-first body, proposed-versus-committed dates. Use for status updates, approval requests, escalations, follow-ups, or when the user only asks to make a message shorter, clearer or less defensive, even without the word email. Produces a subject and body to paste; never sends. Not for casual chat replies; a finished draft can be reformatted for Slack or Teams on request.

findings.evidence: Purpose chooses among Request, Status, FYI, Escalation and Follow-up, then 'Audience only adjusts length and order, never the strategy. Leadership: ... at most 5 sentences' is the only audience default; peer, stakeholder and manager have no length or order default.
findings.fix: Give one default per remaining audience (peer: under 150 words, jargon kept; stakeholder and manager: business effect first, jargon translated) and keep leadership's 5-sentence cap as the exception.

findings.evidence: Step 4 says if facts cannot fit a stated word limit, 'ask (blocking) whether to relax the limit or drop named items', while step 1 says the only blocking gap is no topic and no source draft.

findings.evidence: Eight scenarios cover the main path (approval-request-full-context) and failure paths (empty-request-asks-for-facts, blocked-no-topic-asks-then-stops, word-limit-cannot-fit-facts), but none is an edge case: every prompt is a complete, well-formed scenario.

findings.evidence: The blocking branch 'no topic and no source draft' asks and stops, but the same step then says a pasted email the user received 'is the prior thread, not a draft to rewrite: answer it'. A received email with no topic and no source draft matches both and does not resolve.
findings.fix: Order the branches: if the input is a received message plus an instruction to answer, treat it as the prior thread and draft the reply; only when there is neither a topic, nor a source draft, nor a received message, ask once and stop.

findings.evidence: The description names the task and the not-for neighbour, but it does not say when a bare request such as 'open the PR' or 'write up this branch' should load it without naming a pull request or 'explain PR changes'.
findings.fix: Create or update the GitHub pull request for the current branch from its committed diff: summary, changeset triage, optional Mermaid or draw.io diagram, promotion-branch bodies reused from merged PRs, and reviewers. Use when asked to open, write, refresh or describe a pull request, even as a bare 'open the PR' or 'write up this branch', and for 'explain PR changes', 'open or refresh the PR summary', 'promote develop to main', or 'reuse merged PR bodies'. Pushes feature branches and writes PRs. Not for a read-only explanation of a diff (use explain-changes-mental-model).

findings.evidence: Feature body rules leave the summary and changeset grouping to judgment ('purpose and key changes, at most 150 words', 'group the diff by file into changesets') while the surrounding PR-write path is exact commands. findings.fix: Keep the 150-word and triage rules. Add one default: one changeset per file unless two files change the same exported signature or data flow, in which case they share a changeset; the agent may still split a file that contains two unrelated edits.
